meaning: Observed local failures and bounded recovery; timestamps omitted where the tool transcript did not expose exact event time.

events.event: A byte-hash comparison was initially applied where the saved campaign value was a canonical parsed-object hash. The correct comparison matched; no state change or baseline amendment was made.
An initial read used the wrong allowance module path; the actual execution-allowance module was then read. No runner redesign or alternate launch occurred.

An extra closing bracket prevented script parsing before any saves. The failed script is preserved; only the syntax was corrected. A separate PowerShell quoting parse failure also occurred before mutation.
Nine evidence records saved before a minimum citation guard rejected D70-b. Only the missing D70-b evidence was completed; successful records and dialogue were not regenerated.

events.scope: group-161, group-170 and group-177 tool display
events.event: Tool output was truncated. Manifest inspection confirmed the intended draft/evidence saves had completed; scripts were not blindly rerun.

A tuple-index error left outline values absent. Exact outlines were recovered from the already written literal script rows into explicit v2 records, preserving the original files and actual recovery timestamps. Group-162 recovery was after drafting; group-163 recovery was before drafting.

The citation-length guard stopped at D133-b after five complete assessments and selection of that sixth scene. Recovery skipped all complete records and expanded only the too-short A3/B2 transition citation before completing the missing records.

An unescaped apostrophe prevented the reread script from parsing, before any evidence saves. The subsequent checker correctly rejected missing S04+D166-a candidate evidence. The original failed script is preserved; only the prose quoting was repaired, then all ten previously unwritten assessments were saved and the checker passed.

No technical failure reset an editorial version count or historical allowance. Local semantic repairs have explicit candidate supersession and new same-writer evidence; no prior or new score is represented as fresh review.
